## How to create clips

1. Upload one video (MP4, MOV, MKV, or AVI).
2. Upload two distinct, detailed FaceReader exports (TXT or XLSX), one for each participant. Their **Filename** metadata must match the video, and both exports must use the same frame rate.
3. Optionally adjust **Advanced options** in the sidebar.
4. When all inputs pass validation, select **Process video**. Review clips on the Clips tab, then download the clips ZIP.
5. Clips can be ordered by rank or by time. The default is rank, which is the order of synchrony strength. Time orders clips by their start time in the video.

Clearing inputs removes uploads and previously generated clips. **Reset all inputs** also restores default settings; each advanced panel has its own reset button.

## Advanced options reference

These settings control episode detection, synchrony matching, and clip selection. The defaults are suitable for a first run; adjust them when your study calls for it.

### Clip export

**Number of clips** exports the highest-ranked intervals after emotion and subject selection. Set to `0` to export every episode.

**Buffers before and after** add the requested number of seconds on either side of each selected interval. The exported segment is clipped to the source video boundaries.

**Emotions** keeps only the selected emotions. Leave the selection empty to include all available emotions. Neutral is excluded from synchrony matching, but may be included when selecting individual episodes.

**Optimised subject**: choose `both` to rank shared synchronies by the combined emotion value of both participants, or choose Participant 1 or Participant 2 (named from the uploaded exports’ metadata, falling back to the filename) to rank clips using that participant’s emotion value.

**Only synchronies**: when a single participant is chosen, select shared intervals involving that participant. Clear this option to select that participant’s individual emotion episodes instead. It has no effect when Optimised subject is `both`.

### Synchrony selection

**Time limit** sets a comparison window in seconds from the start of each detected episode. It affects strict and loose constraints; episode uses the full episode span.

**Constraint method**:

- **Strict** ends the comparison at the earlier of the episode end or time limit.
- **Episode** uses the episode’s full end.
- **Loose** extends to the later of those two endpoints.

**Missing threshold** is the minimum proportion of non-missing frames from the comparison participant needed to keep an episode in the synchrony calculation. It ranges from `0` (no minimum) to `1` (all frames present).

### Episode detection

**Entry and exit thresholds**: the entry threshold is the FaceReader emotion value required to enter an episode; the exit threshold is the value below which it ends. Values are probabilities, and the exit threshold must not exceed the entry threshold.

**Delta threshold and delta window** define a minimum increase in emotion value over the chosen time window for the package’s delta/reaction signal. These settings do not set episode boundaries.

**Minimum duration** drops detected episodes shorter than this duration in seconds.

**Consecutive missing frames** sets the maximum run of missing emotion frames tolerated while an episode is active before the episode is ended.

**Cores** controls parallel processing for episode detection and clip encoding. `0` lets the package choose its default worker count; `1` runs clip encoding sequentially.

See the [FaceReader Converter documentation](https://github.com/mmu-research-cloud-platform/facereaderconverter) for the underlying pipeline details.
